edit.description: the clause row's predicate decode normalizes a pre-kebab (snake_case) predicate spelling to its current name at read time
the read test over a lock carrying a snake_case predicate

summary: A committed lock naming a predicate in its pre-kebab spelling (`min_len`) reads as that predicate, never a load fault
acceptance: Per "An upgraded engine owes a committed lock a robust read": a lock whose clause rows spell a predicate in snake_case reads and gates as the kebab-case predicate; the next emit rewrites it canonical. A predicate this engine never named still refuses loud.
tests: a lock naming a predicate in its snake case spelling reads as the kebab case predicate
pins: a lock this engine cannot read is reported as written by another engine
a load fault over another engines lock names both versions and the remedy
a lock carrying the retired max lines predicate refuses at load
notes: Inbox 2026-11-27-old-lock-predicate-rename-load-fault: the v0.0.25 example lock says `min_len`. A renamed spelling normalizes; a retired predicate (max_lines) keeps refusing. Whether the clause id's predicate segment also normalizes before the re-emit is build's call; say which in the body.
